title: Never imagined a president would meddle so directly in a company’s operations.
gist: SemiWiki forum thread reacting to President Trump's direct intervention in Nvidia's operations: posters call it Watergate-level and corruption-driven (citing Trump's Nvidia shareholding), while others argue US presidents have long intervened in companies (GM/Chrysler bailouts, Truman's steel seizure) and that expanding executive power is the root cause.

insights.claim: Forum participants view President Trump's intervention in Nvidia's operations as unusually direct, with one comparing it to Watergate.
insights.speaker: D
insights.so_what: Political entanglement in Nvidia's management is perceived as a governance and reputational risk by industry observers.
insights.quote: This is practically on par with Watergate.

insights.speaker: D
insights.so_what: Nvidia's political alignment may help near-term policy outcomes but ties the stock to administration risk.
insights.quote: Huang: America's unique advantage that no country could possibly have is President Trump.

insights.claim: One poster argues Trump backs perceived winners like Nvidia partly because he profits directly, citing his Nvidia shareholding and broader market-linked gains.

insights.claim: US government intervention in corporations is not unprecedented: Bush and Obama bailed out GM and Chrysler, Carter bailed out Chrysler, and Truman ordered seizure of steel companies in 1952.
insights.speaker: D
insights.so_what: Treat state intervention in strategic firms like Nvidia as a recurring US pattern, not a one-off.

insights.claim: Some participants argue that expanding executive-branch and government power, rather than any single president, is the root cause of increasing political intervention in the economy.
insights.speaker: D
insights.so_what: Expect more, not less, state involvement in strategic industries such as semiconductors regardless of administration.
